card.title: Those Exact Words
card.instruction: Choose one phrase from the interaction and keep returning to what its wording must reveal about the relationship.

transfer.action: I underline two small words beside {prop}.
transfer.opening: You said for now. Why those two words? {request}
transfer.response: For now leaves an expiry date where your welcome should be. {counter}
transfer.challenge: You're reading too much into it.
transfer.closing: Then say for now again without making it sound like a warning.

originalTransfer.action: I underline two small words beside {prop}.
originalTransfer.opening: You said for now. Why those two words? {request}
originalTransfer.response: Still welcome has a lot of space before still. {counter}
originalTransfer.challenge: You're reading too much into it.
originalTransfer.closing: Then help me understand why I can't put those two words down.

card.title: Those Exact Words
card.instruction: Choose one phrase from the interaction and keep returning to what its wording must reveal about the relationship.

originalDialogue.speaker: A
originalDialogue.text: You wrote 'welcome for now.' Why for now?

originalDialogue.speaker: B
originalDialogue.text: I meant you're welcome to stay.

originalDialogue.speaker: A
originalDialogue.text: Then now has brought an unnecessary suitcase.

originalDialogue.speaker: B
originalDialogue.text: You're reading too much into it.

originalDialogue.speaker: A
originalDialogue.text: Too much is another interesting measurement of my welcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your note says I'm 'welcome for now.' Should I unpack?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. I meant until your flat's repaired.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why 'for now' instead of 'until the repairs'? Is your welcome wearing out?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cross it out. You're welcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: But 'for now' was there before I complained. What happens when I stop asking?

card.title: Those Exact Words
card.instruction: Choose one phrase from the interaction and keep returning to what its wording must reveal about the relationship.

originalDialogue.speaker: A
originalDialogue.text: You said we're still friends. Still?

originalDialogue.speaker: A
originalDialogue.text: You can't quietly remove the word after I've heard it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said we're 'still friends' while taking me off the pub quiz team.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Friends. We just need someone who knows sport.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You dropped 'still.' Does that mean friendship's the consolation prize for losing my chair?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Come Thursday anyway. I'll save you a chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell the team we're 'still friends.' I want to hear which word you stress in public.

bindings.scope: Fresh binding-only review of an explicit transfer-body amendment. Read the exact card, both original and accepted candidate single dialogues, and every original/proposed transfer field. Are the proposed fields faithful to the exact mechanism and their described source material? Identify real residual contradictions or unsupported details. Seed hashes still describe the historical originals; validated integration will bind the accepted dialogue only after your compatibility assessment. A compiled transfer is not an individually reviewed pair. Do not score single or pair dialogue; records must be empty. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
